facts.statement: Lusotitan is a large, herbivorous sauropod dinosaur belonging to the Brachiosauridae family that lived in Portugal during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Lusotitan is a genus of herbivorous brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of Portugal.

facts.statement: Lusotitan was a massive sauropod that grew up to 21 meters long and weighed between 25 and 30 tonnes.
facts.quote: Lusotitan was a large sauropod, reaching 21 m in length and 25 - 30 t in body mass.

facts.statement: The animal possessed long forearms with a humerus measuring 2.05 meters and a femur measuring 2 meters.
facts.quote: It had long forearms with the humerus and femur measuring 2.05 m and 2 m in length, respectively.

facts.statement: A large sternal plate found in the fossil record may indicate that Lusotitan reached even larger sizes than the standard measurements suggest.
facts.quote: A large sternal plate that possibly refers to this genus, could indicate larger sizes.

facts.statement: Manuel de Matos discovered large sauropod fossils in the Lourinhã Formation of Portugal in 1947, dating to the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: In 1947 Manuel de Matos, a member of the Geological Survey of Portugal, discovered large sauropod fossils in the Portuguese Lourinhã Formation that date back to the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyszewski originally named the species Brachiosaurus atalaiensis in 1957.
facts.quote: In 1957 Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyszewski named the remains as a new species of Brachiosaurus: Brachiosaurus atalaiensis.

facts.statement: Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes established the separate genus Lusotitan in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003 Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes named it as a separate genus: Lusotitan.

facts.statement: The fossil material consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull and includes vertebrae found in multiple locations.
facts.quote: The finds consisted of a partial skeleton lacking the skull and individual vertebrae uncovered in several locations.

facts.statement: The known remains include 28 vertebrae along with various elements of the appendicular skeleton.
facts.quote: The remains included 28 vertebrae and elements of the appendicular skeleton.

facts.statement: Manuel de Matos, a member of the Portuguese Geological Survey, discovered large sauropod fossils dating to the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic in 1947.
facts.quote: En 1947, Manuel de Matos, miembro del Servicio Geológico de Portugal, descubrió grandes fósiles de saurópodos que se remontan a la etapa Titoniense en el período Jurásico tardío.

facts.statement: Lusotitan fossils were found in the Sobral unit of the Lourinhã Formation, near Atalaia in the municipality of Peralta, Estremadura, Portugal.
facts.quote: Los restos de Lusotitan se encontraron en la unidad Sobral de la Formación Lourinhã, en la municipalidad de Peralta, cerca de Atalaia, en Estremadura, Portugal.

facts.statement: The generic name Lusotitan is derived from the Latin word for an inhabitant of Lusitania and the Greek word for a mythological giant.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva de Luso, el nombre latino para un habitante de Lusitania y de la palabra griega "Titán", un gigante mitológico.

facts.statement: Lusotitan lived in the Lourinhã Formation of western Portugal during the Kimmeridgian or Tithonian ages of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The Lourinhã Formation of western Portugal was likely to be formed during the Kimmeridgian or Tithonian ages of the Late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: Lusotitan lived between 152.21 and 145.06 million years ago, spanning the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: Lusotitan is the largest dinosaur species discovered in the Lourinhã Formation area.
facts.quote: Lusotitan is the largest dinosaur that has been discovered in the area.

facts.statement: Due to similarities with Brachiosaurus, Lusotitan was originally placed within the Brachiosauridae family.
facts.quote: Debido a la similitudes con el Brachiosaurus se colocó dentro de la familia Brachiosauridae.

facts.statement: Later phylogenetic analyses placed Lusotitan as a sister taxon to Titanosauriformes at the base of Macronaria, alongside other Eurasian sauropods like Dongbeititan, Galvesaurus, and Aragosaurus.
facts.quote: posteriores análisis filogenéticos sitúan a Lusotitan como un taxón hermano de Titanosauriformes, en la base de Macronaria junto a otros saurópodos euroasiáticos como Dongbeititan, Galvesaurus y Aragosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2019, Mannion and colleagues re-included Lusotitan in the original Brachiosauridae family.
facts.quote: En 2019 Mannion et al. volvió a incluirlo en el Brachiosauridae original.

facts.statement: Lusotitan coexisted with predatory theropods like Allosaurus and Torvosaurus, the ankylosaurian Dracopelta, other sauropods such as Bothriospondylus and Lourinhasaurus, and stegosaurs including Dacentrurus and Miragaia.
facts.quote: Lusotitan lived alongside species of the predatory theropods Allosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Lourinhanosaurus, and Torvosaurus, the ankylosaurian Dracopelta, the sauropods Bothriospondylus, Lourinhasaurus, and Zby, and the stegosaurs Dacentrurus and Miragaia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Galvesaurus or Galveosaurus are junior synonyms of Lusotitan; while some researchers suggested synonymy in 2017, a 2019 study found distinct characters making them sister taxa.
facts.quote: In 2017, Mocho, Royo-Torres and Ortega suggested that Galvesaurus or Galveosaurus from the Late Jurassic of Spain might represent a junior synonym of this taxon. However, a 2019 description of new material of Galvesaurus by Perez-Pueyo et al. identified phylogenetically informative characters to distinguish it from Lusotitan which was recovered as its sister taxon.

rejected.quote: The area is a coastal region with a strong marine influence.
